overview: Mycenaean is an archaeological term for Late Bronze Age Greek culture, represented by several palatial centers. It does not establish one unified kingdom spanning every site.

items.text: Palace scribes used Linear B to record an early form of Greek. Administrative tablets offer direct evidence of palace organization.
Engineers built bridges, drainage works and irrigation systems. Large-stone masonry also supported fortifications and beehive-shaped tombs.
Workshops made pottery, bronze objects, engraved gems, glass ornaments and precious-metal vessels. Minoan contacts influenced their visual traditions.
Mycenaean pottery traveled widely around the Mediterranean. Oil, wine and other contents were probably important reasons for transporting the vessels.
Mycenae and Tiryns preserve monumental walls, while Mycenae's Lion Gate and corbelled tombs show different solutions to building with heavy stone.
Destruction and palace decline spread during the late thirteenth century BCE. The surviving evidence does not supply one named conqueror or a single fall date for all centers.
